answer: Use a rotating audit committee chosen by a verifiable random function: each epoch, a small committee is drawn unpredictably from established identities, and every new claim must pass review before it pays out. Members stake reputation on each approval, and a false approval slashes both submitter and approvers, so creating many fake identities cannot buy a seat at the summit of trust. One fraud finding sends a ripple across the committee's past approvals, triggering re-checks, while the horizon for newcomers stays capped until their work survives several independent committees.
